prompt:
## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Membership Number
where: MemberRepository (uses), src/persistence/memberRepository.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
return this.members.get(membershipNumber);
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B
concept: Membership
where: ReportService (uses), src/business/reportService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
if (b.membershipNumber !== undefined) row.membersAdmitted += b.tickets;
=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: A is the Membership Number, an identifier that MemberRepository uses as its lookup key ("return this.members.get(membershipNumber);", src/persistence/memberRepository.ts). B is Membership, the broader member relationship or status. ReportService (src/business/reportService.ts) infers it from whether a booking has a membership number ("if (b.membershipNumber !== undefined) row.membersAdmitted += b.tickets;"). Both use the same field, but an identifier and the thing it identifies are different concepts. Under the rule that sharing an id does not make two concepts the same, they are not the same. This is borderline, because B's evidence is entirely the membershipNumber attribute.
